assertion: It marks the third straight year of record-breaking passenger volume for the rail operator.
independent_value: Release says third straight year; FY25 34.5M was second consecutive record

assertion: Amtrak said this week that it hit a record 37.1 million riders over the past year, a 7.4% jump fueled in part by Americans ditching expensive flights and high gas prices.
source_finding: Gas and airfare CPI both rose sharply in FY26, so the mechanism is plausible; but Amtrak's release credits new trains, infrastructure, Acela, World Cup and America250 and never mentions fuel or fares, gross ticket revenue rose only 1%, and FY25 grew 5.1% while gas fell.
inaccuracy: Figures are accurate; the 'fueled by' attribution rests on one executive's belief and is not shown by the data, and gas prices spiked only from March 2026, about five months into the fiscal year
why_not: The 7.4% figure matches the release; the grade applies only to the causal clause.
sql: SELECT AVG(price_dollars_per_gallon) FROM energy.eia_retail_gasoline_prices WHERE series_id='EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG' AND report_date>='2025-10-01' AND report_date<'2026-10-01'
